I'm 61 years old, and I've been farming in Quzhou County all my life. I only went to primary school, but I know my land better than any book-smart person ever could. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I've been growing wheat and maize in rotation for over 40 years, and that's what I'll stick with. I don't trust new crops that I'm not familiar with — I need to feed my family and have something solid to sell.

Winter wheat is the backbone of my farm. I'll plant it in October right after the National Day holiday. I'll buy improved seeds from the county seed station — I've used Jinmai 47 and Shimai series before, and they do well here. I'll put about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, maybe 10 kg of phosphorus, and about 8 kg of potassium. My land is decent but needs fertilizer. I'll irrigate the wheat four times: overwintering water, jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water. That's what I've always done. I'll do rotary tillage before sowing to prepare a good seedbed, and I'll spray pesticides twice — once for weeds and once for aphids or rust if they show up. I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather cooperates.

After the wheat harvest in early June, I won't waste a single day. I'll immediately plant summer maize — hybrid seeds, usually Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. These have served me well. The maize gets about 20 kg nitrogen per mu, plus some base fertilizer. I'll irrigate three times: at seedling stage, jointing, and filling. I'll till with rotary before sowing. Two pesticide sprays should handle any armyworms or borers. I expect around 550 kg per mu of maize. This double-cropping system is exhausting, but it's the only way I know to make the most of my land.
